xs-setup(1) ​

Getting started

Build the binary, install it locally, and make your first transfer.

NAME ​

xs-setup — build and install xs from the xsync source checkout.

REQUIREMENTS ​

Python 3, a C++20 compiler, CMake, zstd, xxHash, and ICU are required. Ninja is used by the build examples. Run the commands below from the xsync source directory.

PlatformDependencies
macOSApple command-line developer tools; Homebrew libraries
LinuxC++20 compiler; development packages for zstd, xxHash, and ICU

BUILD ​

macOS dependencies
sh
brew install cmake ninja zstd xxhash icu4c
Debian / Ubuntu dependencies
sh
sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build python3 libzstd-dev libxxhash-dev libicu-dev
Build and inspect the binary
sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
build/xs --version

INSTALL ​

Local installation
sh
cmake --install build --prefix "$HOME/.local"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

This installs the executable, the generated manpage, and zsh completion. Add the PATH setting to your shell configuration if you want it to persist.

zsh completion — put before your existing compinit setup
sh
fpath=("$HOME/.local/share/zsh/site-functions" $fpath)
autoload -Uz compinit
compinit

FIRST TRANSFER ​

Copy source contents into the destination
sh
xs -aP src/ dst/

Replace both paths with your own. Progress is automatic when stderr is a terminal; -P also preserves partial transfer data for a later retry.

RELEASE BUILDS ​

Build release artifacts
sh
cmake --preset release-static
cmake --build --preset release-static

The release flow produces Linux amd64/arm64 binaries and a macOS universal binary. A macOS host is needed for the macOS output; the documented macOS build also requires Docker, GNU make, and the toolchain. A Linux host can build Linux outputs.
